title: Phased Data Migration
summary: Migrate data in successive waves (by product, region or entity), with source and target coexisting and synchronised during the transition.
body_markdown:
# Phased Data Migration

## Problem

A single cut-over is too risky or impossible within the available downtime.

## Context

Large or business-critical migrations; systems that can coexist.

## Forces

- Risk reduction vs. cost and complexity of coexistence.

## Solution

Partition the data into waves. For each wave: migrate, reconcile, switch users/processes. Keep source and target synchronised (e.g. [[Change Data Capture]] or dual write) for data shared across waves.

## Architecture

```text
Legacy ──wave 1..n migration──▶ Target
   ▲  ◀──── synchronisation (bidirectional where needed) ────┘
```

## Advantages

- Smaller blast radius; learning between waves.

## Disadvantages

- Coexistence complexity; longer total duration; temporary interfaces.

## Risks

- Synchronisation errors; wave boundaries that cut through shared entities.

## When to Use

- High risk, limited downtime, separable data.

## When Not to Use

- Tightly coupled data that cannot be partitioned; small volumes.

## Alternatives

[[Big Bang Data Migration]].

## Examples

- Migrating policies product line by product line.

## Related Decisions

- [[Select Data Migration Approach]]
